raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On Intel XPU, video inputs are decoded on the host CPU; this decodes them on the GPU media engine through the torchcodec-xpu plugin, as CUDA already does with NVDEC.

## Usage

`SGLANG_ENABLE_XPU_VIDEO_HW_DECODE=1` (default `0`, opt-in): on XPU, with torchcodec-xpu installed, video inputs decode on the media engine and the frames stay on the XPU. Decoded frames need memory headroom on the card, so pick a `--mem-fraction-static` that leaves room. Without it, or on other platforms, decode stays on the CPU as before.

## Accuracy Tests

Decoded frames match CPU decode within colour-conversion rounding (max 2 levels, XPU hardware test). The Qwen3-VL video e2e test passes on XPU.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Intel Arc Pro B60, torch 2.14.0+xpu, torchcodec-xpu 0.17.0.

| Workload | Hardware decode off | On |
|---|---|---|
| Decode 60 frames of 720p, standalone | 482 ms, 9.8 CPU-s | 471 ms, 0.1 CPU-s |
| Qwen3-VL-2B, 32 video requests, conc 8: server CPU per request | 22.8 s | 7.8 s |
| Qwen3-VL-2B, conc 8: requests/s | 0.27 | 0.24 (no gain; run-to-run noise 14%) |
| Gemma-4 E2B, conc 8: requests/s | 1.25 | 1.63 |
| Gemma-4 E2B, conc 8: TTFT p50 | 4.20 s | 2.33 s |
| Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B, TP 4, conc 1: tokenizer CPU per request | 19.0 s | 4.0 s |
| Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B, TP 4, conc 1: requests/s | 0.07 | 0.07 |

Prefill-bound models (Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-Omni) gain host CPU, not throughput; models with a short prefill (Gemma-4) gain end to end. Decoded frames use device memory outside `--mem-fraction-static`, so the docs advise headroom on the decoding card.

Related: #42627 (open) also adds torchcodec-xpu, pinned to 0.15.0 for torch 2.13; main needs 0.17.0. #44966 (open) moves device calls onto `current_platform`, which `_parallel_decode` follows here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation according to Write documentations.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+# Benchmarks sglang's VideoDecoderWrapper on a clip: CPU torchcodec with the
+# default parallel decoders versus the accelerator path (CUDA NVDEC or Intel
+# XPU media engine through torchcodec-xpu). Reports wall and process CPU time.
+#
+# == Usage Examples ==
+#
+# python3 bench_video_decode.py --clip clip.mp4 --device xpu --num-frames 60
+# python3 bench_video_decode.py --clip clip.mp4 --device cuda --dense
+
+import argparse
+import time
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils.video_decoder import VideoDecoderWrapper
+
+
+def _sync(device: str) -> None:
+    if device != "cpu":
+        torch.get_device_module(device.split(":")[0]).synchronize()
+
+
+def _run(clip: str, device: str, indices: list[int], iters: int):
+    with VideoDecoderWrapper(clip, device=device) as w:
+        w.get_frames_as_tensor(indices[:1])  # warm up
+        _sync(device)
+        wall, cpu = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
+        for _ in range(iters):
+            out = w.get_frames_as_tensor(indices)
+            _sync(device)
+        wall = (time.perf_counter() - wall) / iters
+        cpu = (time.process_time() - cpu) / iters
+        return wall, cpu, str(out.device)
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--clip", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--device", default="xpu", help="cuda, xpu or xpu:N")
+    parser.add_argument("--num-frames", type=int, default=60)
+    parser.add_argument("--dense", action="store_true", help="decode every frame")
+    parser.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=3)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    with VideoDecoderWrapper(args.clip, device="cpu") as probe:
+        total, fps, (h, w) = len(probe), probe.avg_fps, probe.frame_shape
+    if args.dense:
+        indices = list(range(total))
+    else:
+        indices = np.linspace(0, total - 1, args.num_frames, dtype=int).tolist()
+    print(
+        f"clip: {total} frames @ {fps:.1f} fps, {w}x{h}; decoding {len(indices)} frames"
+    )
+    print(
+        f"{'requested -> decoded on':<28}{'wall ms':>10}{'CPU ms':>10}{'frames/s':>10}"
+    )
+    for device in ("cpu", args.device):
+        wall, cpu, out_device = _run(args.clip, device, indices, args.iters)
+        print(
+            f"{device + ' -> ' + out_device:<28}"
+            f"{wall * 1e3:>10.0f}{cpu * 1e3:>10.0f}{len(indices) / wall:>10.0f}"
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

 and sent via the command line (e.g. using `curl`) or via your own script.
 
+## Hardware Video Decoding for Multimodal Models
+
+Video inputs for vision-language models (for example Qwen3-VL and Gemma 4) can decode on the Intel GPU media engine through the [torchcodec-xpu](https://pypi.org/project/torchcodec-xpu) plugin. It is off by default; set `SGLANG_ENABLE_XPU_VIDEO_HW_DECODE=1` to turn it on. torchcodec loads the plugin automatically, decoded frames stay on the XPU as `uint8` tensors, and the resize and normalization steps of the processor run on the same device. SGLang runs one hardware decode at a time per process. Without the plugin, or on GPUs without a media engine such as Intel Data Center GPU Max, decoding runs on the CPU.
+
+The plugin is part of the XPU dependency manifest (`python/pyproject_xpu.toml`) and the XPU Docker image. For a manual install, match the versions pinned there and make sure the system FFmpeg libraries are built with VAAPI support:
+
+```bash
+pip install torchcodec==0.17.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu --no-deps
+pip install torchcodec-xpu==0.17.0 --no-deps
+```
+
+Environment variables:
+
+| Variable | Default | Effect |
+|---|---|---|
+| `SGLANG_ENABLE_XPU_VIDEO_HW_DECODE` | `0` | Set to `1` to decode video inputs on the media engine. Other platforms never read this. |
+| `SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODES` | `1` | Hardware decodes allowed at once per process. |
+| `SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_HW_MAX_FRAMES` | `128` | The first video sampling more frames than this switches the process to CPU video decode. |
+
+torchcodec and the plugin have their own settings: `TORCHCODEC_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` stops torchcodec from loading device plugins, and torchcodec-xpu's `CPU_FALLBACK=off` makes unsupported codecs raise instead of silently decoding on the CPU.
+
+Decoded frames live in device memory outside the scheduler's `--mem-fraction-static` budget, roughly 170 MB per 60 sampled 720p frames plus the processor's pixel tensors. Leave headroom on the card for the number of videos you expect in flight at once; with the card full, decode and preprocessing slow down by an order of magnitude instead of failing.
+
+Hardware decode is validated for sparse sampling, up to roughly 100 frames per video. With dense sampling (for example `--mm-process-config '{"video": {"fps": 4, "max_frames": 512}}'` on long clips), the first time a video samples more than `SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_HW_MAX_FRAMES` frames (default 128), SGLang switches the process to CPU video decode and logs it once.
+
+SGLang logs a warning once if the plugin reports that it fell back to CPU decoding. To check the engine directly, run `benchmark/video_decode/bench_video_decode.py --clip <file> --device xpu` and compare the CPU time of the two rows.
+
 ## XPU Graph [Experimental]
 
 SGLang enables XPU graph capture to reduce per-step kernel-launch overhead.

+"""Intel XPU hardware video decode policy for :class:`VideoDecoderWrapper`.
+
+torchcodec loads the Intel plugin (PyPI ``torchcodec-xpu``) through its
+``torchcodec.backends`` entry point, so ``VideoDecoder(..., device="xpu")`` is
+the whole integration. This module decides whether that device is used, how
+many hardware decodes may run at once, and when to fall back to the CPU; the
+wrapper keeps its existing RuntimeError -> CPU fallback.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+import logging
+import threading
+from functools import lru_cache
+from typing import Optional
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# One decoder per codec engine; Arc Pro B60/B70 expose two (xe fdinfo drm-engine-capacity-vcs).
+XPU_DECODERS_PER_CARD = 2
+
+_dense_video_seen = False
+_decode_slots: Optional[threading.BoundedSemaphore] = None
+_decode_slots_lock = threading.Lock()
+_fallback_warned = False
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def xpu_video_decode_device() -> Optional[str]:
+    # Bare "xpu" is the current device, where the HF fast image processor already runs.
+    from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+    from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_xpu
+
+    if (
+        _dense_video_seen
+        or not is_xpu()
+        or not envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_XPU_VIDEO_HW_DECODE.get()
+    ):
+        return None
+    if importlib.util.find_spec("torchcodec_xpu") is None:
+        logger.info(
+            "torchcodec-xpu is not installed; video inputs decode on the CPU. "
+            "Install torchcodec-xpu to use the XPU media engine."
+        )
+        return None
+    return "xpu"
+
+
+def xpu_decoders_per_video() -> int:
+    return min(XPU_DECODERS_PER_CARD, _max_concurrent_decodes())
+
+
+def xpu_decode_slot() -> threading.BoundedSemaphore:
+    # WORKAROUND(torchcodec-xpu): intel/torchlib-xpu#161; see SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODES.
+    global _decode_slots
+    with _decode_slots_lock:
+        if _decode_slots is None:
+            _decode_slots = threading.BoundedSemaphore(_max_concurrent_decodes())
+    return _decode_slots
+
+
+def note_video_frames(num_frames: int) -> bool:
+    # WORKAROUND(torchcodec-xpu): intel/torchlib-xpu#162. Process-wide and sticky,
+    # since a dense video stalls the hardware decodes of every video in the process.
+    global _dense_video_seen
+    from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+    if _dense_video_seen:
+        return True
+    limit = envs.SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_HW_MAX_FRAMES.get()
+    if num_frames <= limit:
+        return False
+    _dense_video_seen = True
+    xpu_video_decode_device.cache_clear()
+    # Nothing reuses the cached frame blocks after the switch, and xe evicts
+    # instead of failing allocations, so torch would never trim them.
+    import torch
+
+    torch.xpu.empty_cache()
+    logger.info(
+        "A video samples %d frames (> SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_HW_MAX_FRAMES=%d); video "
+        "inputs decode on the CPU from now on in this process.",
+        num_frames,
+        limit,
+    )
+    return True
+
+
+def warn_once_on_cpu_fallback(decoder) -> None:
+    # The plugin falls back silently by default (CPU_FALLBACK=on).
+    global _fallback_warned
+    if _fallback_warned:
+        return
+    status = decoder.cpu_fallback
+    if status:
+        _fallback_warned = True
+        logger.warning(
+            "torchcodec-xpu fell back to CPU decoding (%s); video inputs are "
+            "not using the XPU media engine.",
+            status,
+        )
+
+
+def _max_concurrent_decodes() -> int:
+    from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+    return max(1, envs.SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODES.get())

+"""Device selection and output contract of ``VideoDecoderWrapper``.
+
+The torchcodec boundary is faked so the assertions check what the wrapper
+asks torchcodec for and what it hands back, not whether a mock was called.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt import platforms
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.utils import common
+from sglang.srt.utils import video_decoder as vd
+from sglang.srt.utils import video_decoder_xpu
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _FakeTorchcodecDecoder:
+    """Stands in for ``torchcodec.decoders.VideoDecoder``.
+
+    Frames are reported on the requested device; a device listed in
+    ``failing_devices`` raises the RuntimeError torchcodec raises when a
+    device backend cannot open the source.
+    """
+
+    failing_devices: set = set()
+    num_frames = 8
+    cpu_fallback = (
+        False  # torchcodec's CpuFallbackStatus is falsy when decoding on the device
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self, source, **kwargs):
+        device = kwargs.get("device", "cpu")
+        if device in self.failing_devices:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"no decoder for {device}")
+        self.kwargs = kwargs
+        self.metadata = SimpleNamespace(average_fps=30.0, height=4, width=6)
+        self._device = torch.device("meta" if device != "cpu" else "cpu")
+
+    def _frames(self, n):
+        return torch.zeros((n, 4, 6, 3), dtype=torch.uint8, device=self._device)
+
+    def __len__(self):
+        return self.num_frames
+
+    def __getitem__(self, idx):
+        return SimpleNamespace(data=self._frames(1)[0])
+
+    def get_frames_at(self, indices):
+        return SimpleNamespace(data=self._frames(len(indices)))
+
+
+class _FakeDeviceModule:
+    """Stands in for torch.xpu / torch.cuda on hosts without the accelerator."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def current_device():
+        return 0
+
+
+class _FakePlatform:
+    """Stands in for current_platform, whose device calls need real hardware."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def get_device(device_id=0):
+        return f"fake:{device_id}"
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def set_device(device):
+        pass
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _patched(*, xpu_ok, failing=()):
+    """Fake the torchcodec and accelerator-runtime boundaries for the duration."""
+    _FakeTorchcodecDecoder.failing_devices = set(failing)
+    with (
+        patch.object(vd, "VideoDecoder", _FakeTorchcodecDecoder, create=True),
+        patch.object(vd, "_BACKEND", "torchcodec"),
+        patch.object(vd, "_try_cuda_backend", lambda: True),
+        patch.object(vd, "_try_xpu_backend", lambda: xpu_ok),
+        patch.object(torch, "get_device_module", lambda device_type: _FakeDeviceModule),
+        patch.object(platforms, "current_platform", _FakePlatform, create=True),
+    ):
+        yield
+
+
+def _wrapper(device, *, xpu_ok, failing=()):
+    with _patched(xpu_ok=xpu_ok, failing=failing):
+        return vd.VideoDecoderWrapper(b"not-a-real-video", device=device)
+
+
+class TestVideoDecoderWrapperDevice(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_xpu_decoders_per_video_follow_the_concurrency_limit(self):
+        # The default of 1 concurrent hardware decode means one decoder, not 16 CPU-style ones.
+        self.assertEqual(_wrapper("xpu", xpu_ok=True)._num_decode_threads, 1)
+        with envs.SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODES.override(2):
+            w = _wrapper("xpu", xpu_ok=True)
+            self.assertEqual(
+                w._num_decode_threads, video_decoder_xpu.XPU_DECODERS_PER_CARD
+            )
+        with envs.SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODES.override(8):
+            # Never more decoders per video than codec engines per card.
+            self.assertEqual(
+                video_decoder_xpu.xpu_decoders_per_video(),
+                video_decoder_xpu.XPU_DECODERS_PER_CARD,
+            )
+
+    def test_xpu_requested_without_plugin_decodes_on_cpu(self):
+        w = _wrapper("xpu", xpu_ok=False)
+        self.assertNotIn("device", w._tc_kwargs)
+        self.assertEqual(w._num_decode_threads, 0)
+
+    def test_xpu_open_failure_falls_back_to_cpu(self):
+        with _patched(xpu_ok=True, failing={"xpu:1"}):
+            w = vd.VideoDecoderWrapper(b"not-a-real-video", device="xpu:1")
+            self.assertNotIn("device", w._tc_kwargs)
+            self.assertIsInstance(w.get_frames_at([0, 1]), np.ndarray)
+
+    def test_cpu_frames_are_numpy(self):
+        with _patched(xpu_ok=True):
+            w = vd.VideoDecoderWrapper(b"not-a-real-video", device="cpu")
+            self.assertIsInstance(w[0], np.ndarray)
+            self.assertIsInstance(w.get_frames_at([0, 1]), np.ndarray)
+
+    def test_accelerator_frames_stay_tensors(self):
+        with (
+            _patched(xpu_ok=True),
+            envs.SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODES.override(2),
+        ):
+            w = vd.VideoDecoderWrapper(b"not-a-real-video", device="xpu")
+            frame = w[0]
+            batch = w.get_frames_at([0, 1, 2])
+            # Three indices over two decoders exercises the split-and-concat path.
+            tensor = w.get_frames_as_tensor([0, 1, 2])
+        for value in (frame, batch, tensor):
+            self.assertIsInstance(value, torch.Tensor)
+            self.assertNotEqual(value.device.type, "cpu")
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(batch.shape), (3, 4, 6, 3))
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(tensor.shape), (3, 4, 6, 3))
+
+
+class TestDenseVideoMovesToCpu(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):

+
+    def test_dense_video_moves_itself_and_the_process_to_cpu(self):

+            patch.object(common, "is_xpu", lambda: True),
+            envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_XPU_VIDEO_HW_DECODE.override(True),
+        ):
+            self.assertIsNone(video_decoder_xpu.xpu_video_decode_device())
+
+    def test_sparse_video_stays_on_xpu(self):
+        with _patched(xpu_ok=True), envs.SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_HW_MAX_FRAMES.override(100):
+            w = vd.VideoDecoderWrapper(b"not-a-real-video", device="xpu")
+            self.assertNotEqual(w.get_frames_at(list(range(60))).device.type, "cpu")
+
+    def test_dense_video_off_xpu_keeps_its_device(self):
+        with _patched(xpu_ok=False), envs.SGLANG_XPU_VIDEO_HW_MAX_FRAMES.override(100):
+            for device in ("cuda", "cpu"):
+                w = vd.VideoDecoderWrapper(b"not-a-real-video", device=device)
+                before = dict(w._tc_kwargs)

+                self.assertEqual(w._tc_kwargs, before)
+
+

+"""Video decode on the Intel XPU media engine through torchcodec-xpu.
+
+Checks the frames ``VideoDecoderWrapper`` and ``load_video`` return on XPU,
+compares them with the CPU decode, and records the CPU-time saving so a
+regression to CPU decoding fails the test rather than only slowing it.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+import os
+import tempfile
+import time
+import unittest
+
+import av
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_xpu, load_video
+from sglang.srt.utils.video_decoder import VideoDecoderWrapper
+from sglang.srt.utils.video_decoder_xpu import xpu_video_decode_device
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, is_in_ci, write_github_step_summary
+
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=60, suite="stage-a-test-1-gpu-xpu")
+
+_WIDTH, _HEIGHT, _FPS, _SECONDS = 1280, 720, 30, 10
+_SAMPLED = 60  # 2 fps over the clip, the Qwen-Omni sampling pattern
+
+
+def _synthesize_h264_clip(path: str) -> None:
+    """Moving-gradient H.264 clip; libx264 ships with PyAV's FFmpeg."""
+    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:_HEIGHT, 0:_WIDTH]
+    with av.open(path, mode="w") as container:
+        stream = container.add_stream("libx264", rate=_FPS)
+        stream.width, stream.height, stream.pix_fmt = _WIDTH, _HEIGHT, "yuv420p"
+        stream.options = {"preset": "ultrafast", "g": "30"}
+        for i in range(_FPS * _SECONDS):
+            frame = np.stack(
+                [(xx + 3 * i) % 256, (yy + 2 * i) % 256, (xx // 4 + yy // 4 + i) % 256],
+                axis=-1,
+            ).astype(np.uint8)
+            packets = stream.encode(av.VideoFrame.from_ndarray(frame, format="rgb24"))
+            for packet in packets:
+                container.mux(packet)
+        for packet in stream.encode():
+            container.mux(packet)
+
+
+def _timed(fn):
+    wall, cpu = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
+    out = fn()
+    return out, time.perf_counter() - wall, time.process_time() - cpu
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(is_xpu(), "Intel XPU not available")
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    importlib.util.find_spec("torchcodec_xpu") is not None,
+    "torchcodec-xpu plugin not installed",
+)
+class TestVideoDecoderXPU(CustomTestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        cls.clip = os.path.join(cls.tmpdir.name, "clip.mp4")
+        _synthesize_h264_clip(cls.clip)
+        cls.indices = np.linspace(0, _FPS * _SECONDS - 1, _SAMPLED, dtype=int).tolist()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def tearDownClass(cls):
+        cls.tmpdir.cleanup()
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.enterContext(envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_XPU_VIDEO_HW_DECODE.override(True))
+        xpu_video_decode_device.cache_clear()
+        self.addCleanup(xpu_video_decode_device.cache_clear)
+
+    def test_wrapper_decodes_on_xpu(self):
+        with VideoDecoderWrapper(self.clip, device="xpu") as w:
+            self.assertEqual(w._tc_kwargs.get("device"), "xpu")
+            self.assertEqual(len(w), _FPS * _SECONDS)
+            self.assertAlmostEqual(w.avg_fps, _FPS, places=2)
+            self.assertEqual(w.frame_shape, (_HEIGHT, _WIDTH))
+            frames = w.get_frames_at(self.indices[:4])
+            tensor = w.get_frames_as_tensor(self.indices[:4])
+        for value in (frames, tensor):
+            self.assertIsInstance(value, torch.Tensor)
+            self.assertEqual(value.device.type, "xpu")
+            self.assertEqual(value.dtype, torch.uint8)
+            self.assertEqual(tuple(value.shape), (4, _HEIGHT, _WIDTH, 3))
+
+    def test_load_video_uses_xpu_when_enabled(self):
+        with load_video(self.clip, use_gpu=True) as w:
+            self.assertEqual(w._tc_kwargs.get("device"), "xpu")
+            self.assertEqual(w[0].device.type, "xpu")
+
+    def test_env_switch_forces_cpu_decode(self):
+        with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_XPU_VIDEO_HW_DECODE.override(False):
+            xpu_video_decode_device.cache_clear()
+            with load_video(self.clip, use_gpu=True) as w:
+                self.assertNotIn("device", w._tc_kwargs)
+                self.assertIsInstance(w.get_frames_at([0, 1]), np.ndarray)
+
+    def test_xpu_frames_match_cpu_decode(self):
+        with VideoDecoderWrapper(self.clip, device="xpu") as gpu:
+            on_xpu = gpu.get_frames_at(self.indices[:8]).cpu().numpy()
+        with VideoDecoderWrapper(self.clip, device="cpu") as cpu:
+            on_cpu = cpu.get_frames_at(self.indices[:8])
+        diff = np.abs(on_xpu.astype(np.int16) - on_cpu.astype(np.int16))
+        # Different YUV->RGB converters (VAAPI/SYCL vs swscale) round differently.
+        self.assertLess(diff.mean(), 1.0)
+        self.assertLessEqual(diff.max(), 8)
+
+    def test_xpu_decode_saves_cpu_time(self):
+        def decode(device):
+            with VideoDecoderWrapper(self.clip, device=device) as w:
+                out = w.get_frames_as_tensor(self.indices)
+                if out.device.type != "cpu":
+                    torch.xpu.synchronize()
+                return out
+
+        decode("xpu")  # warm the media engine and the plugin
+        _, xpu_wall, xpu_cpu = _timed(lambda: decode("xpu"))
+        _, cpu_wall, cpu_cpu = _timed(lambda: decode("cpu"))
+        summary = (
+            f"### XPU video decode ({_SAMPLED} frames of {_WIDTH}x{_HEIGHT} H.264)\n"
+            "| path | wall ms | CPU ms |\n|---|---|---|\n"
+            f"| CPU torchcodec (sglang parallel decoders) | {cpu_wall * 1e3:.0f} | {cpu_cpu * 1e3:.0f} |\n"
+            f"| XPU media engine (torchcodec-xpu) | {xpu_wall * 1e3:.0f} | {xpu_cpu * 1e3:.0f} |\n"
+        )
+        print(summary)
+        if is_in_ci():
+            write_github_step_summary(summary)
+        # CPU time is the stable signal on shared runners; wall time is not.
+        # Measured ~30x less on Arc Pro B60, so 0.5 leaves room for slow hosts.
+        self.assertLess(xpu_cpu, 0.5 * cpu_cpu)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""Qwen3-VL video chat completion on Intel XPU.
+
+Video frames decode on the XPU media engine (torchcodec-xpu) and flow into
+the on-device resize and HF fast processor. The shared video mixin supplies
+the clip and the content assertions used by the CUDA VLM suite.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_xpu
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
+from sglang.test.vlm_utils import VideoOpenAITestMixin
+
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=600, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu")
+
+XPU_SERVER_ARGS = [
+    "--device",
+    "xpu",
+    "--tp=1",
+    "--disable-overlap-schedule",
+    "--page-size",
+    "64",
+    "--mem-fraction-static",
+    "0.70",
+    "--attention-backend",
+    "intel_xpu",
+]
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(is_xpu(), "Intel XPU not available")
+class TestQwen3VLVideoXPU(VideoOpenAITestMixin):
+    model = "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct"
+    extra_args = XPU_SERVER_ARGS
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        # The server process inherits the override, so it decodes on the media engine.
+        with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_XPU_VIDEO_HW_DECODE.override(True):
+            super().setUpClass()
+
+
+# Delete the mixin class so that unittest/pytest do not collect it on its own.
+del VideoOpenAITestMixin
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
